meaning: to argue a position you do not necessarily hold, in order to test the strength of an idea
literal_translation: bir fikrin sağlamlığını test etmek için karşıt görüşü bilerek savunmak
example: I'll play devil's advocate and question whether the survey really proves your point.
origin: Comes from the Catholic Church's office of 'advocatus diaboli', an official who argued against a candidate's sainthood to test the case

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pretend to be evil in order to frighten others
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with evil or frightening people; it refers only to arguing a counter-position in debate.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to avoid making any decision in a discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes actively arguing one side of an issue, not avoiding a decision.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to agree with everyone in a group discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which involves deliberately challenging the prevailing view.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' comes from a historical Church role in which an official argued against a proposed sainthood. Today it means arguing the opposing side on purpose to test an idea's strength.
